partners.diseaseBName: mitochondrial complex V (ATP synthase) deficiency, nuclear type 4A
partners.mechanism_chain: PMPCA (HGNC:24126) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial protein import and assembly (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial protein import and assembly (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0046933); ATP5F1A (HGNC:8542) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0046933); Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0046933) —LEADS_TO→ Ataxia (HP:0001251); Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0046933) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency (HP:0003200). Loss-of-function mutations in PMPCA disrupt mitochondrial protein import and assembly, indirectly impacting mitochondrial ATP synthesis. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in ATP5F1A directly impair mitochondrial ATP synthesis. Both disruptions converge on the central process of mitochondrial ATP synthesis, leading to overlapping phenotypes such as ataxia and general mitochondrial dysfunction.

partners.diseaseBName: hypermetabolism due to uncoupled mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation 2
partners.mechanism_chain: ATP5F1B (HGNC:1000) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial ATP synthase complex assembly and function (GO:0045277); Mitochondrial ATP synthase complex assembly and function (GO:0045277) —LEADS_TO→ Hypermetabolism (HP:0002101); PMPCA (HGNC:29244) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial ATP synthase complex assembly and function (GO:0045277); Mitochondrial ATP synthase complex assembly and function (GO:0045277) —LEADS_TO→ Spinocerebellar ataxia (HP:0007127). #### 1. mitochondrial complex V (ATP synthase) deficiency, nuclear type 4A  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.518)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1268020, Reactome:R-HSA-9837999)

**Proposed mechanism:** PMPCA (HGNC:24126) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial protein import and assembly (GO:0005759); Mitochondrial protein import and assembly (GO:0005759) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0046933); ATP5F1A (HGNC:8542) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0046933); Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0046933) —LEADS_TO→ Ataxia (HP:0001251); Mitochondrial ATP synthesis (GO:0046933) —LEADS_TO→ Mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency (HP:0003200). Loss-of-function mutations in PMPCA disrupt mitochondrial protein import and assembly, indirectly impacting mitochondrial ATP synthesis. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in ATP5F1A directly impair mitochondrial ATP synthesis. Both disruptions converge on the central process of mitochondrial ATP synthesis, leading to overlapping phenotypes such as ataxia and general mitochondrial dysfunction.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of shared phenotypes like ataxia or mitochondrial dysfunction in patients with biallelic loss-of-function mutations in PMPCA or ATP5F1A respectively would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD within the coding regions of PMPCA and ATP5F1A that do not segregate with disease in affected families.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared reliance on mitochondrial ATP synthesis could lead to therapeutic strategies aimed at boosting mitochondrial function or mitigating energy deficits in patients with either disease.
